subject: NetSeat private deployment commissioning intake — network & ops checkpoints
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah@netseat.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+security@netseat.com, procurement@netseat.com
Date: 2028-06-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: NetSeat private deployment — commissioning intake and ops checkpoints

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for taking NetSeat as a private deployment customer — excited to get started. Attached is our initial intake export (netseat-intake-sheet.csv) with requested environment details. For the commissioning sprint we want to align on the network items and operational checkpoints so we don't hit surprises during cutover.

Top asks from our side:
- VPC peering vs. interconnect options (we have a dedicated circuit but can also peer).
- Egress IP model and static IPs for allowlisting (we need 4 stable egress IPs).
- Bastion / jumpbox access pattern, preferred ports and port-forwarding rules.
- KMS/HSM integration: we use AWS KMS CMKs in our account — ask if Redwood needs key grants or to bring keys.
- Audit/evidence: we will want an ops runbook and SLAs for fallback behavior.

Can you confirm which of these you need answers to up-front, and propose an intake checklist (we can iterate) plus an initial 60-minute kickoff next week?

Regards,
Sarah Li
Head of Cloud Operations, NetSeat

Attachments: netseat-intake-sheet.csv
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah@netseat.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NetSeat private deployment — commissioning intake and ops checkpoints

Hi Sarah — thanks for the intake. I pulled the CSV and skimmed the initial rows — helpful.

Quick replies to your bullets:
- Peering vs. interconnect: Either works. For predictable latency we recommend a dedicated interconnect where available; peering is OK for expedited onboarding. We will include both options in the intake checklist.
- Egress IPs: We can allocate 4 static egress IPs from the Redwood side or you can provide a NAT gateway with static Elastic IPs on your side. Both patterns supported; I'll have Ben sketch the IP allocation options.
- Bastion: Our standard pattern is SSH bastion + short-lived certs for engineers and a separate service account for automation. We'll detail ports and port-forwarding rules in the playbook.
- KMS: We support customer-managed CMKs. We'll need an IAM grant (AWS) or equivalent key policy to allow Redwood to encrypt/decrypt model keys in a limited scope. Kimberly will own the KMS checklist.
- Ops runbook/SLA: I'll attach a Redwood commissioning playbook draft and a proposed mutual-action-plan.xlsx with milestones and owners.

Proposed next steps:
1) Kickoff: 60 min — Tue 2028-06-14 10:00 PT or Wed 2028-06-15 09:00 PT (pick one).
2) NetSeat to confirm network topology + CIDR ranges before kickoff.
3) Redwood to provide playbook + egress IP options in 48 hours.

Ben / Kimberly: can you review the intake (attached) and add any immediate must-haves, then I will send a meeting invite.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Architect — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-commissioning-playbook.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx
From: Sarah Li <sarah@netseat.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+security@netseat.com, procurement@netseat.com
Date: 2028-06-11T15:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NetSeat private deployment — commissioning intake and ops checkpoints

Thanks Hannah — Wed 6/15 09:00 PT works for us.

Quick clarifications from our firewall/ops lead:
- We'll prefer NetSeat-hosted NAT (Elastic IPs in our account) for compliance reasons, but we may ask Redwood to provide a short-term set of public egress IPs for smoke testing.
- Our security team asks for an inbound allowlist for the Redwood management plane (we'll need the list before cutover).
- We also need a simple temporary escalation contact list for on-call conflicts during the first 72 hours after cutover.

I'll bring our network diagram to the kickoff. Looking forward to the playbook.

Sarah

Hannah — thanks. A few engineering notes after I reviewed their intake:

- CIDR size: NetSeat listed 10.40.0.0/16 for application subnets. That's fine, but recommend reserving at least /24 for management and /24 for logging (we should call out exact subnets in the MAP).
- Egress: If NetSeat is providing EIPs, ensure they reserve 6 addresses: 4 for data egress, 1 for bastion management, 1 spare for cutover fallback.
- NAT & SNAT: If we host NAT on our side we can map 4 logical egress IPs to session pools; if they host NAT we need their ASN and BGP details if going interconnect.
- Ports: Allow SSH 22 for bastion; management plane uses 443 + 5222 (agent). We should list required ports per role in the runbook.

Karthik — can you validate the proposed CIDR carve and quickly produce an egress-ip suggestion file we can attach to the MAP? If we host egress we will need to allocate public IPs from our pool and create an egress assignment artifact.

Ben
Principal Deployment Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-13T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NetSeat private deployment — commissioning intake and ops checkpoints

Ben / team — quick return. I validated the CIDR carve: recommend the following allocation (example):
- 10.40.0.0/24 — management (bastion, monitoring)
- 10.40.1.0/24 — logging/telemetry
- 10.40.2.0/23 — application tier

Egress IPs: attached egress-ip-allocation.txt with 6 candidate IPs from Redwood's pool for the case we must host egress during smoke. If NetSeat keeps NAT, we need their EIP list and BGP peering windows.

Other quick checklist items I marked 'must have' before kickoff:
- IAM roles and a service account for automation (least privilege).
- KMS key ARN and the principal to grant (we will not store unwrapped key material).
- Confirmation on required telemetry retention (30/90/365 days).

I will upload the egress file to the MAP folder and add comments to the commissioning playbook.

Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Runtime & Connectivity
Redwood Inference
